name: live_full_join_makes_both_sides_nullable
description: FULL JOIN makes NOT NULL columns on BOTH sides nullable, since a row can be unmatched in either direction. Joins users to tags rather than users to orders: orders.user_id carries a foreign key to users, so no order can ever be unmatched and the join would degenerate to a LEFT JOIN, proving only half the rule.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE users (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now())
CREATE TABLE tags (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE)
query_sql:
-- @name GetUsersFullJoinedToTags
-- @returns :many
SELECT u.name AS user_name, t.name AS tag_name FROM users u FULL JOIN tags t ON u.id = t.id ORDER BY COALESCE(u.id, t.id)

columns.name: user_name
columns.note: NOT NULL in schema but nullable: a tag with no matching user leaves the whole users side NULL

columns.name: tag_name
columns.note: NOT NULL in schema but nullable: a user with no matching tag leaves the whole tags side NULL

sqlc_comparison.sqlc_behavior: sqlc keeps both sides non-nullable, so a FULL JOIN generates two fields that are both wrong
sqlc_comparison.scythe_improvement: scythe marks both sides nullable, and this fixture seeds genuinely unmatched rows on each side so the engine returns a NULL in both columns

default: INSERT INTO users (id, name, email) VALUES (1, 'Ada Lovelace', 'ada@example.com')
INSERT INTO users (id, name, email) VALUES (2, 'Grace Hopper', 'grace@example.com')
